bull.b: Conversion of design wins into mass production provides tangible revenue visibility beyond initial development cycles. A growing production base and backlog extending into 2027 can support scale, customer retention, and stronger utilization of Sequans' cellular IoT platform.

bull.t: Cleaner balance sheet after debt repayment
bull.b: Eliminating convertible and COVID-related debt reduces refinancing, interest, and dilution risks while improving financial flexibility. The cleaner capital structure allows management to direct resources toward product development, customer support, and scaling its core IoT semiconductor business.

bull.t: Product-led growth and expanding connectivity opportunities
bull.b: Product-led growth is more repeatable than one-off licensing revenue and indicates increasing adoption of Sequans' connectivity solutions. New RF, drone, defense, and industrial opportunities broaden the addressable market and may create additional recurring product revenue.

bear.b: The scale of current losses shows that revenue is not yet sufficient to support the operating structure. Volatility between prior profitability and subsequent heavy losses makes earnings quality difficult to assess and increases execution risk as the company pursues growth.

Ongoing cash consumption limits Sequans' ability to self-fund product expansion and increases reliance on asset sales, financing, or successful licensing transactions. Even with improved liquidity, a durable positive operating cash-flow inflection has not yet been demonstrated.

Lower product margins and prolonged supply constraints can restrict operating leverage as volumes grow. Dependence on unpredictable licensing agreements for revenue upside adds volatility, making the path to breakeven reliant on both cost control and successful commercial execution.
